questions.question: Under the optimized continuous-flow conditions for vinylcarbazole dimerization, which combination did the authors identify as optimal?

options.A: 0.5 mL min−1 flow, 20 min residence time, 2 mol% catalyst, and 450 nm irradiation
options.B: 0.1 mL min−1 flow, 100 min residence time, 0.1 mol% catalyst, and 405 nm irradiation
options.C: 2 mL min−1 flow, 5 min residence time, 1 mol% catalyst, and 420 nm irradiation
options.D: 0.5 mL min−1 flow, 20 min residence time, 4.5 mol% catalyst, and 405 nm irradiation

questions.rationale: The optimization section identifies 0.5 mL min−1 (τ=20 min), 2 mol% catalyst, and 450 nm as the optimal flow conditions.
questions.evidence_quote: Optimal synthesis of 1 was realized at a flow rate of 0.5 mL.min -1 ( = 20 min) with a catalyst loading of 2 mol % (entry 1) with irradiation at 450 nm.

questions.question: What happened when the flow rate was reduced to 0.1 mL min−1 during the vinylcarbazole dimerization, and what cause did the authors propose for the accompanying carbazole?

options.A: Yield rose to 98%, and carbazole formed by direct thermal rearrangement of the cyclobutane
options.B: Yield fell to 53%, and longer residence time increased oxygen-mediated background oxidation of vinylcarbazole
options.C: Yield fell to 79%, and catalyst photobleaching produced carbazole
options.D: Yield remained near 93%, and carbazole arose from hydrolysis of the catalyst

questions.rationale: At 0.1 mL min−1 (100 min residence time), product yield dropped to 53%; the authors associated carbazole formation with adventitious oxygen and longer exposure.
questions.evidence_quote: flow rate was reduced to 0.1 mL.min -1 ( = 100 min) where the yield of 1 dropped to a very modest 53% (entry 6).

questions.question: Which control experiments established that the flow dimerization required both the organophotoredox catalyst and illumination?

options.A: Removing either catalyst 10 or irradiation prevented the dimerization
options.B: Removing catalyst reduced yield by 10%, while removing light increased conversion
options.C: Removing catalyst gave the same yield, but removing light slowed the reaction to five days
options.D: The catalyst-free reaction proceeded only at 405 nm, while the dark reaction required oxygen

questions.rationale: The authors report no dimerization when catalyst 10 was absent and also no dimerization without irradiation.
questions.evidence_quote: The dimerization did not proceed in the absence of 10 (entry 9) nor in the absence of irradiation (entry 10).

questions.question: For the 10 mmol preparation of t-DCzCB, what catalyst loading and isolated yield did the flow procedure achieve?
questions.rationale: The scale-up used 0.1 mol% of catalyst 10 and furnished t-DCzCB in 79% isolated yield.
questions.evidence_quote: Finally, the dimerization was performed at 10 mmol scale of 2 using only 0.1 mol% of 10 at 0.5 mL.min -1 providing t-DCzCB 1 in 79% isolated yield (entry 11).

questions.question: How did the continuous-flow outcome for 3-bromo-9-vinylcarbazole compare with the batch result?

options.A: Flow at 0.2 mL min−1 gave 64% isolated yield in a shorter run, versus 48% in batch after five days
options.B: Flow gave 48% after five days, versus 64% in a one-hour batch reaction
options.C: Flow failed to form product, whereas batch gave 64% after five days
options.D: Flow gave 31%, versus 71% in batch, with both completed in under an hour

questions.rationale: The 3-bromo substrate gave 48% in batch after five days, while flow at 0.2 mL min−1 produced 64% isolated yield in 50 min residence time.
questions.evidence_quote: Three flow rates were trialed for the continuous flow conditions with 12a with 0.2 mL.min -1 ( = 50 min) providing 12b in an improved isolated yield of 64%.

questions.question: Which positional bromine substitution was reported to resist cyclobutane formation under both the batch and flow conditions?
questions.rationale: The 1-bromo-9-vinylcarbazole substrate was unusually challenging and no cyclobutane product was detected in either mode.
questions.evidence_quote: In contrast, 1-bromo-9-vinylcarbazole (15a) proved a very challenging substrate to dimerize using both batch and continuous flow conditions with no observed cyclobutane product (15b) being detected by 1 H NMR analysis.

questions.question: Which substrate-specific combination illustrates the authors' chemoselective conversion of a bis-vinylated hydroxycarbazole derivative?

options.A: The bis-vinylated 20a formed the bis-enol-ether cyclobutane 21b in 25% isolated yield
options.B: The bis-vinylated 20a formed the brominated dimer 14b in 65% isolated yield
options.C: The mono-vinylated 19a formed the bis-enol-ether cyclobutane 21b in 45% isolated yield
options.D: The bis-vinylated 20a formed t-DCzCB in 79% isolated yield

questions.rationale: Vinylation of 2-hydroxycarbazole gave 20a; its selective dimerization furnished bis-enol-ether cyclobutane 21b, albeit in modest yield.
questions.evidence_quote: dimerization of 20a provided the cyclobutyl bis-enolether 21b, albeit in a modest isolated yield of 25%

questions.question: What downstream transformations did the authors use to demonstrate the synthetic utility of brominated cyclobutylcarbazoles?

options.A: Suzuki coupling of 13b gave product 25 in 75%, and palladium-mediated borylation gave 26 in 36%
options.B: Hydrogenation of 13b gave 25 in 36%, and oxidation gave 26 in 75%
options.C: Suzuki coupling gave 26 in 75%, and borylation gave 25 in 36%
options.D: Direct photolysis of 13b gave 25 in 65%, and chlorination gave 26 in 50%

questions.rationale: The paper describes a Suzuki cross-coupling of 13b yielding 25 at 75% and a palladium-mediated borylation yielding 26 at 36%.
questions.evidence_quote: A palladium mediated Suzuki crosscoupling of the 13b with 4-methoxybenzene boronic acid using the conditions of Kumar and Tao 15 provided the cyclobutane 25 in a yield of 75%.

questions.question: How did the authors address the modest flow yield for 4-methoxystyrene dimerization, and what yield did the additive-assisted example give?

options.A: They added 0.25 equivalents of anthracene as an electron relay; the 4-methoxystyrene dimer was isolated in 44%
options.B: They added 0.25 equivalents of diethylaniline as a radical inhibitor; the dimer was isolated in 75%
options.C: They switched to 0.1 mol% catalyst at 405 nm; the dimer was isolated in 79%
options.D: They increased the residence time to 100 min without additive; the dimer was isolated in 53%

questions.rationale: Anthracene was used as an electron relay and improved product outcome; the paper reports 44% isolated dimer for 4-methoxystyrene under flow.
questions.evidence_quote: Introduction of 4-methoxy styrene (27) into the continuous flow conditions provided the dimer 28 in a modest isolated yield 44%.

questions.question: What was the reported outcome for scale-up dimerization of E-asarone to magnosalin, and which reaction feature distinguished it from traditional batch organophotoredox conditions?

options.A: A 10 mmol flow run gave 40% isolated magnosalin without cryogenic temperatures and in a shorter time
options.B: A 1 mmol batch run gave 79% isolated magnosalin only at cryogenic temperature
options.C: A 10 mmol flow run gave 22% isolated magnosalin but required a five-day reaction
options.D: A 10 mmol batch run gave 40% isolated magnosalin using 3 mol% catalyst at cryogenic temperature

questions.rationale: The paper reports E-asarone dimerization with anthracene on 10 mmol scale, giving magnosalin in 40% isolated yield; flow avoided cryogenic conditions and shortened the reaction.
questions.evidence_quote: E-aserone (3) was then successfully dimerized, again using anthracene as an electron relay, on a 10 mmol scale providing the lignan magsosalin 4 in 40% isolated yield.
